gardner_synopsis: The mostly destroyed leaves 283-284 perhaps contained the end of chapter 117, certainly the whole of chapter 118, and the beginning of chapter 119. Only a few words may be read, and no overall sense of the contents is achievable.
editorial_notes: Chapter title is lost (given as '[ ... ]' in the raw extract). Teaching text is extremely fragmentary; lacunae are preserved exactly as given. Page artifacts were normalized by converting '(283)' and '(284)' to manuscript page markers ⟨p.283⟩ and ⟨p.284⟩. Coptic line-break markers '/' were removed inside lacunae brackets by collapsing sequences like '[ ... / ... ]' to '[ ... ]' without altering the lacuna indication. Embedded manuscript line numbers (5, 11, 14, 15, 19, 25) were retained because they occur within lacuna brackets and may belong to the fragment as presented; no safe separation from potential content is possible in this damaged context.
